lede: ANSWR is a home-salon beauty brand run by Owow OÜ, a company registered in Tallinn, Estonia, that ships UK orders from a UK warehouse. Its best-known product is an at-home keratin treatment. Here's what it sells, what its Trustpilot and store reviews say, the complaints that repeat, and who it suits.

parts: ANSWR is a real company with a working Shopify store, published shipping and refund policies and a 30-day money-back guarantee. Trustpilot showed a 3.9 TrustScore from about 1,750 reviews when we checked, and its own review page lists 2,247 reviews. Most buyers like how smooth their hair turned out; the complaints that repeat are slow dispatch, results that didn't last for some hair types, and slow replies to refund requests.

Home versions of salon treatments. The main one is the at-home keratin treatment (£37.90 a bottle): you spray it on clean, dry hair, leave it for an hour, rinse, dry and seal it with a straightener at 180°C. ANSWR says it is formaldehyde-free, vegan, and lasts up to three months from one application; those are the brand's claims. It also sells a kit with post-treatment shampoo and conditioner (£49.90), the shampoo and conditioner in 300ml bottles (£39.90), an exfoliating hair removal drop (£24.90), a flyaway and brow control stick (£17.90), the Volumewave heated brush (£79.90) and DIY lash extension kits.

The keratin treatment's ingredient list includes glyoxylic acid and fragrance. If you have sensitive skin, read the full list on the product page first, and the brand suggests covering your shoulders with an old towel because the formula can mark coloured fabric.

parts.small: Checked on November 25, 2026. The store's review page is run by the brand, so treat it as a showcase rather than an independent score.

parts: Positive reviews come from people with wavy, frizzy or curly hair who say it went smooth and shiny, cut their styling time and lasted around three months, some saying 3.5. Several compare it favourably with salon keratin treatments on price.

The negative Trustpilot reviews describe orders that took nearly two weeks to be dispatched, hair that went back to frizzy after the first wash, hair that felt dry or smelled bad after the treatment, and refund requests left unanswered. Some reviewers also say the company replied and refunded them. Results vary by hair type, so it's worth reading reviews from people whose hair is like yours.

Yes. It's a registered company with a UK and a Netherlands warehouse, tracked Royal Mail delivery in the UK, a written refund policy and thousands of reviews across Trustpilot and its own store. The fair question is whether the treatment works on your hair, not whether your order will arrive. Keep your order number and photos if you plan to use the money-back guarantee, and pay by card or PayPal for buyer protection.

A salon keratin treatment usually costs much more than £37.90, so if one bottle gives you the months of smoothness the brand describes, it's good value: by ANSWR's own count that's about £0.49 a day. If your hair is very curly or you only want a one-off, read the negative reviews first: some buyers didn't get lasting results. The subscription (£29.90 a bottle) and the 2 pack bring the price down if you use it regularly.

Is the ANSWR keratin treatment worth it?
If it lasts the up to three months the brand describes, £37.90 is far less than a salon treatment. Some reviewers didn't get lasting results, so read reviews from people with hair like yours.

ANSWR says up to three months from one application. Reviewers report anything from about 3.5 months to results fading after the first wash.

An at-home keratin treatment and kit, post-treatment shampoo and conditioner, an exfoliating hair removal drop, a flyaway and brow control stick, a heated brush and DIY lash extensions.
